newsitem.title: UK: YTT aims to regain lost advertising share.
newsitem.headline: YTT aims to regain lost advertising share.

text.p: Britain's Yorkshire-Tyne Tees Television Holdings Plc said on Tuesday that its share of independent television (ITV) advertising revenue was not satisfactory and that it was determined to restore it to past levels.

But YTT chairman Ward Thomas said that he was confident that the company could look forward to continuing growth in the current year. YTT reported 1996 pre-tax profit of 30.2 million pounds ($48.49 million), a rise of 40 percent.
YTT aims to regain lost advertising share =2
YTT said its 1996 advertising sales were "disappointing", falling to 10.31 percent of total ITV advertising revenue -- more than 12 million pounds below expectations at the start of the year.

The company said revenue growth of more than five percent in the first quarter of this year gave it greater confidence that it could achieve the 10.9 percent ITV revenue share forecast by Laser, its advertising sales agent.
But it said that it was determined to restore the higher levels of past years. Chairman Thomas has said previously that a return to a 14 percent share should be YTT's target.

But his overall message was upbeat. "With rising advertising revenue and share, a strong forward order book for programming and costs under firm control, I am confident that your company can look forward to continuing growth in the current year," Thomas said. ($1=.6228 Pound)
